cards.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
cards.titleEn: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
cards.summary: In his first interview since being forced from his post, Gen Syrskyi speaks about Ukraine's future in the war. Gen Syrskyi, pictured here in Donetsk region in April 2026, lost his job over the summer after a public disagreement with the defence minister Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC. Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer. He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

cards.title: ‘My son was killed’ France faces backlash over proposed police firearms law
cards.titleEn: ‘My son was killed’ France faces backlash over proposed police firearms law
cards.summary: As protests nationwide protests rage, activists warn proposed law could lead to more impunity. As protests rage across France, activists warn proposed law could deepen impunity. Paris, France – Issam El Khalfaoui’s teenage son Souhail was shot and killed by a police officer in 2021 in Marseille. “When my son was killed during a police traffic stop, we realised how difficult it was to bring the truth to light. The police and the justice system took different actions to cover up the evidence. We realised that this was a deeply systemic issue,” El Khalfaoui told Al Jazeera. “The IGPN [National Police] lost the video that captured my son’s murder. The witnesses were not interviewed, and the case file completely disappeared from the court. That is the reality.” France has one of the highest numbers of fatal police shootings in Western Europe. At least 69 people were killed by police or gendarmerie officers in 2024, compared with 49 in 2023 and 50 in 2022.

cards.title: UK growth forecast upgraded but higher energy prices to hit economy next year
cards.titleEn: UK growth forecast upgraded but higher energy prices to hit economy next year
cards.summary: The prediction from the IMF comes as final preparations are being made for the first Budget under Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The UK economy is forecast to grow by more than previously expected this year before higher energy prices and interest rates hit the economy in 2027, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said. The organisation's latest report, which is closely watched by the government, said the UK economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027. Economies across the world have proved more resilient to the energy price shock caused by the US-Iran war, the IMF said, but it warned the economic fallout from the conflict remained "highly uncertain". Chancellor John Healey said the government would look to "provide some breathing space" for households in the Budget.

cards.title: Super El Niño sets another record as it strengthens to 'unprecedented levels'
cards.titleEn: Super El Niño sets another record as it strengthens to 'unprecedented levels'
cards.summary: El Niño has continued to strengthen, with several key measures now in record territory. Simon King explores how it compares to previous events. Flooded streets following the arrival of Hurricane Polo in the town of Puerto San Carlos, Baja California Sur, Mexico, on 29 September. The Category 3 storm added to an already busy hurricane season turbo-charged by El Niño. El Niño has continued to strengthen to what some scientists are calling "unprecedented levels", weeks before its expected peak in December. In its latest update, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) said average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific have reached their highest level on record , external . It comes after scientists declared a new record for daily sea surface temperatures in the central-eastern Pacific in September, exceeding the previous record set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

cards.titleEn: S. Korea maintains demand for Ukraine's apology over N.K. POW disclosure
cards.summary: SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- South Korea is continuing efforts to resolve its recent diploma... This will let Google show Yonhap news articles that match or are related to your search "The government hopes that all pending issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon told a press briefing. "To that end, we will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side and are currently maintaining communication." The statement came after Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the matter had been "resolved" in an interview with RBC-Ukraine on Monday (local time). "Everything stemmed from different interpretations of the confidentiality requirements at various stages of the transfer of the prisoners of war. Ukraine fulfilled all its obligations," Sybiha was quoted as saying by RBC-Ukraine.
